summary: Time-bound multi-account console access for on-call runbook edits
description:
Issue summary: The on-call playbook for the inference serving layer requires a small set of edits to adjust recovery steps for the new autoscaler integration. Reporter (Marta Ruiz) requests console access across three cloud accounts (prod-aws-main, prod-aws-aux, and prod-gcp-primary) for two engineers on the on-call rotation so they can update the runbook entries and validate links.

Impact: Low functional risk to customers, but the edits are time-sensitive — the runbook currently references deprecated autoscaler knobs that cause confusion during incidents. Lack of timely edits prolongs mean time to recovery for certain P1 throttling scenarios.

Requested access model: Temporary, time-bound console access using least-privilege roles mapped to SSO groups. Access windows: single 8-hour session per engineer (non-recurring) on 2026-03-03 between 09:00-17:00 US/Eastern. Required permissions: view/edit runbook storage (Confluence and runbook repo PRs), read access to autoscaler metrics dashboards, read-only to serving runtime and scheduler resources, and ability to create a small config PR in the ops-configs repo. No long-lived credentials.

Justification: Engineers on rotation need to fix inaccurate steps that have already caused a 22m longer SLO recovery during last week's incident. Security review requested and approved with constraints below.

Provisioning steps requested: 1) Create two timebound cross-account IAM roles in prod-aws-main and prod-aws-aux with a AssumeRole policy scoped to Okta SAML group tag 'oncall-temp-editors'. 2) Create equivalent short-lived IAM Service Accounts (with Workload Identity Federation) in prod-gcp-primary mapped to the same Okta group. 3) Set TTL to 8 hours and enforce MFA via SSO session requirements. 4) Attach a managed policy limiting access to specific resource ARNs and CloudWatch/Cloud Logging read scopes.

Expiry & audit: All temporary assume-role events must be recorded in CloudTrail and exported to the security S3 bucket; access logs retained for 90 days. A post-access verification checklist must be filled by the assignee and attached to this ticket.

Security constraints: No ability to alter IAM policies, KMS keys, or billing; no creation of new long-lived roles; no console-wide admin. Any attempt to elevate must be blocked and logged.

Notes: This is an internal support request and not customer-facing. Link to affected runbook page and patch suggestions included in comments.
investigation_notes: Checked existing IAM role catalogs and found no pre-existing 'oncall-temp-editors' mapping in aws-org STS trust policies. Verified Okta group exists (okta:/groups/oncall-temp-editors) and contains the two engineers. Confirmed CloudTrail delivery to s3://redwood-security-logs is healthy. Confirmed ops-configs repo has an open PR template that requires branch protection (so PR creation is safe). Security approved via #security-approvals with timestamp 2026-03-02T15:20Z. Determined required policy scoping to be minimal: describe/list EC2/ASG/Autoscaling read, CloudWatch/GetMetricData read, CloudWatch Logs read, GCP Monitoring read, and Confluence page edit via Atlassian API token (handled separately).
comments: Marta Ruiz (Reporter) 2026-03-01: Requesting timebound console access for two rotation engineers: Ethan Cole and Lina Park. See proposed edits attached as gist: https://gist.github.com/mruiz/oncall-runbook-diff

Priya Desai (Assignee) 2026-03-01: Acknowledged. I will coordinate with Cloud Infra and Security to create timebound roles. Confirming target accounts: prod-aws-main, prod-aws-aux, prod-gcp-primary. Any objection to 8-hour TTL?

Lina Park (Security) 2026-03-01: Security approves 8-hour TTL with MFA enforced via Okta session. Ensure CloudTrail logging to security bucket is active and that role ARN is whitelisted for no policy-change permissions.
Ethan Cole (SRE) 2026-03-02: Confirmed both engineers already have Okta 2FA and are in the oncall-temp-editors group. Also request read access to autoscaler dashboards in Datadog (prod).

Priya Desai 2026-03-02: Actions taken: created IAM role 'redwood-oncall-temp-editors' in prod-aws-main and prod-aws-aux with AssumeRole for Okta SAML provider, attached scoped read-only policy. Created GCP service account 'redwood-oncall-temp-editors@prod-gcp-primary' and bound Workload Identity with Okta group. Configured STS TTL to 8 hours. Added CloudTrail filter to export events for these roles to s3://redwood-security-logs/temp-access/INT-7623/
Lina Park 2026-03-03: Verified CloudTrail and GCP Audit logs show no policy modification calls during the session. MFA enforced. Audit copy uploaded to Confluence with link in resolution notes.

Priya Desai 2026-03-03: Requester confirmed runbook edits applied and PR merged in ops-configs. Closing temporary access per policy. Follow-up assigned to INT-7624 for automating temporary role issuance.
resolution_notes: Provisioning completed on 2026-03-02: - AWS roles 'arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/redwood-oncall-temp-editors' and 'arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-oncall-temp-editors' created with 8h TTL and scoped read permissions. - GCP service account redwood-oncall-temp-editors@prod-gcp-primary with Workload Identity configured. - Okta SAML group 'oncall-temp-editors' mapped and enforced MFA. - CloudTrail and GCP Audit logs exported to s3://redwood-security-logs/temp-access/INT-7623/ and archived. - Edit PR in ops-configs merged (https://github.com/redwood/ops-configs/pull/703). Post-action verification completed by Lina Park; no suspicious activity observed. Follow-up: INT-7624 (Task) to automate ticket-driven temporary role creation via our internal access bot, and INT-7625 to add runbook unit tests to prevent future stale instructions.
